text:
harper (People Ops): Dropping a follow-up here from the all-hands Q&A — focused on promos, comp timing, and a few process clarifications. Will update as we get questions.
ellis (People Ops): Key bullets: promo approvals -> calibration -> final signoff. Goal: changes effective first of next month. Payroll/process caveats below.
devon (Eng): If calibration happens and I get approved mid-cycle, is my manager expected to notify me immediately or wait for the official letter?
harper (People Ops): Managers should let people know verbally as soon as approval is confirmed. Official promotion letter will come from People Ops within 3 business days after signoff.
fran (Finance): Note on payroll: if approval is after payroll cutoff (25th PT), base salary update will apply to the following payroll; any retro will show as an adjustment line. Payroll-bot will post line-item details.
payroll-bot: FYI: Retro adjustments labeled "Promo Retro - [Name]"; taxed as normal income; net pay reflected in the payroll run two cycles after approval if post-cutoff.
devon (Eng): That "two cycles" bit is concerning — can you clarify?
fran (Finance): Sure. If approval comes after cutoff for payperiod A, then base pay updates for payperiod B but retro covering payperiod A is processed and may land in payperiod B or C depending on timing — we aim for B but sometimes it needs an extra run. Well escalate urgent cases.
sanjay (CTO): On managerial best practices: document two concrete impact examples in the packet. When in doubt, show trajectory and clear ownership expansion. That really helps committee decisions.
ellis (People Ops): Calibration checklist well publish today: 1) two impact examples; 2) peer feedback (optional but helpful); 3) manager assessment vs rubric; 4) recommended comp movement. Pasteable 1:1 checklist will be in manager kit.
nora (Recruiting): Hiring + promotion question: if promo shifts comp band up, does that reduce headcount for hiring approvals? Weve seen confusion when backfills are requested.
harper (People Ops): Promotion itself doesn't automatically consume headcount. Backfill requests still go through the normal intake flow. If comp movement creates budget pressure, Finance may flag it for review but we won't block the promotion decision for headcount.
devon (Eng): Appeals — what's the timeline if someone disagrees with the committee outcome?
ellis (People Ops): Appeals are possible. Step 1: raise with your manager and people partner. Step 2: submit appeal form (link posted below). Appeals reviewed by a 3-person cross-functional panel. Target turnaround: 10 business days.
harper (People Ops): Link: https://company.share/promotion-appeal-form (internal).
devon (Eng): Are there any changes to equity refresh eligibility tied to promotions this cycle?
ellis (People Ops): No policy change this cycle. Equity refreshes are decoupled and handled by Talent Comp — you will get communications separately.
sanjay (CTO): Also adding: when writing examples, focus on measurable outcomes (latency improvements, cost saved, feature adoption numbers) where possible. Numbers help.
fran (Finance): For above-band approvals there is an extra Finance review step; typical SLAs: 3-5 business days. Please include business rationale in the packet to speed it up.
harper (People Ops): Quick note on confidentiality: managers should coordinate announcements with the employee. Default flow: team-first, then company announcement via People Ops template. If you need assistance drafting a post, DM People Ops.
devon (Eng): Can People Ops share a short template for the manager verbal + written note?
ellis (People Ops): Yep — manager verbal script + email template and Slack blurb will be uploaded to the manager kit by EOD. Example snippet: "Congrats — effective [date], your new title/level is X. Your new base is $Y and youll see retro in payroll if applicable."
harper (People Ops): Open enrollment/benefits question from earlier: no change to window dates. Benefits team will post FAQ and 1:1 office hour schedule next week.
nora (Recruiting): One practical thing — when a promotion opens a higher pay band, hiring for that level in the next 30 days: is there a recommended reviewer to avoid conflicting approvals?
harper (People Ops): Flag the role in the hiring intake form with a note "recent internal promo impacted band" and tag your finance partner. That helps expedite review.
devon (Eng): Thanks everyone. One last thing: can People Ops confirm the promo timeline publicly in #engineering so managers know the cutoff?
ellis (People Ops): Will post a short FAQ and the hard cutoff (25th) in #engineering and drop the manager kit link.
harper (People Ops): Thanks all — keep questions here or DM People Ops if private. Well update the thread with the final manager kit link.
